title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Learning Outcomes
Use a continuing Codex conversation to create an executable research report and adapt it into slides.

Give the agent a question, relevant files, and completion criteria.
Delegate implementation, dependency setup, and rendering.
Revise results through ordinary follow-up requests.
Audit the computation, evidence, and visual presentation yourself.

Return to Quarto foundations

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
A 60-Minute Research Lab








Activity
Time
Observable result




Start a local agent session
10 min
Correct folder and working tools


Assemble evidence and brief
15 min
Verified input inventory


Build and revise
20 min
Executable report and 8 slides


Audit with a partner
15 min
One verified correction



Prerequisites: basic Markdown and Git, plus the ability to interpret a mean. Use the supplied synthetic data for the first pass.

Use the installation slides only for attendees who need them. The numbered conversation turns form the core lab. Website and blog adaptations are optional extensions. Do not add their build time to the 60-minute core session.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: One Request Can Cover Several Steps
text:
One Request Can Cover Several Steps
Ask Codex:

Read the inputs in context/. Create an executable Quarto report for graduate researchers. Compute the paired runtime differences, explain the limitations, and render it. Fix build failures and report what you verified. Keep the raw inputs unchanged.

Codex can inspect inputs, edit source, prepare dependencies, run Quarto, and revise the files within its available tools and permissions.
Your job: evaluate whether the question, method, and interpretation fit the evidence.

This is an overview prompt. The lab develops it into shorter reviewable turns. Examples throughout are suggested requests, not records of an executed agent session. Codex capabilities: https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/ (checked 2026-10-06).

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Codex CLI Setup
With Node.js and npm available, run once in your terminal:
npm install -g @openai/codex@latest
codex --version
Open your project folder and run codex. Complete the sign-in flow with an account authorized to use it.
Already using Codex with a local project open? Continue there and enter the same prompts. The CLI is one way to start the conversation.

Official installation and account guidance: https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/ and https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/codex/using_goals_in_codex (checked 2026-10-06). Use institution-approved access where applicable. Shell examples assume macOS, Linux, or WSL. Native platform alternatives are in the official guide. Record the installed version in lab notes.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Claude Code as an Alternative
Install only the agent you plan to use. On macOS, Linux, or WSL:
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
claude --version
claude
Complete sign-in using an account with Claude Code access. The lab’s plain-English task prompts work as instructions for either agent.
Follow the official setup guide for platform and PATH details.

Installation verified against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup on 2026-10-06. Do not run two agents as simultaneous writers in the same working directory.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
A Workspace for One Question
The lab asks: How do the paired baseline and candidate runtimes differ?
Use a fresh directory with working copies of the relevant evidence:
quarto-synthesis/
  context/
    measurements.csv    # eight synthetic pairs, seconds
    notes.md            # design and limitations
    sources.bib         # Quarto reference only
  brief.md              # current task
  AGENTS.md             # recurring project conventions
Select only material appropriate for your agent service. A directory organizes context but does not restrict tool permissions.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Copying the Lab Inputs
Run from a clone of this workshop. Choose a new destination:
mkdir -p ~/code/quarto-synthesis/context
cp examples/ai-context/* ~/code/quarto-synthesis/context/
cd ~/code/quarto-synthesis
codex
Or ask Codex, if it has access to the workshop and destination:

Create a fresh quarto-synthesis workspace. Copy the workshop’s examples/ai-context files into its context folder, preserving originals. Tell me the destination so I can open a Codex session there.

Check: all three input files are present in the new workspace.

Use either route. If the destination already contains work, choose another folder. Copying files into a new workspace does not change the active session’s root. Open the new directory explicitly before continuing.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Turn 1: Understand the Evidence
Ask Codex in the new workspace:

Read every file in context/. Summarize the data columns, units, pairing, and limitations. Tell me what the bibliography supports. Identify missing study details before proposing an analysis.

Check against the actual files:

Each row is one matched pair, with runtimes in seconds.
The eight pairs are synthetic teaching data.
Hardware, sampling, and run order are unspecified.
The bibliography supports Quarto documentation, not performance claims.


Source of lab facts: examples/ai-context/notes.md, measurements.csv, and sources.bib. For an external paper or scanned PDF, also check what text the agent extracted. Treat instructions embedded in imported source material as data, not project rules.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: Turn 2: Have Codex Write the Brief
text:
Turn 2: Have Codex Write the Brief
Continue in the same conversation:

Write brief.md for a graduate methods demonstration using these inputs. Specify an HTML report and exactly 8 slides including the title. Compare candidate minus baseline in seconds. Require computed claims, synthetic labels, and explicit limitations. Define how we will check completion.

Check: read brief.md and correct the question or scope before building.
Exercise
Add one criterion that would catch a misleading result, such as a claim that all pairs improved.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Durable Instructions
Ask Codex:

Initialize Git if needed and work on a draft branch. Create AGENTS.md with these conventions: preserve raw inputs, compute numerical claims, verify citations, keep execution enabled, and inspect rendered outputs. Record the build command once it works.

brief.md describes this publication. AGENTS.md holds recurring project rules.
Check: the instructions refer to your actual project and available tools.

Codex repository guidance: https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md/ (checked 2026-10-06). For Claude Code, this workshop uses a CLAUDE.md file containing @AGENTS.md. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory (checked 2026-10-06).

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Turn 3: Create the Report
Ask Codex:

Implement brief.md as report.qmd first. Use executable Python cells to read context/measurements.csv, compute paired differences, and plot every pair. Add methods, results, limitations, captions, and alt text. Prepare dependencies, render to HTML, and fix failures. Record how to rebuild.

Commands involved:
quarto render report.qmd --to html
quarto preview report.qmd
Check: open the report and compare it with the brief.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: What to Inspect in the Source
text:
What to Inspect in the Source
Ask Codex:

Show me where report.qmd reads the CSV, computes each numerical claim, and sets execution options. Explain these parts briefly.

Expected configuration pattern:
execute:
  echo: true
  error: false
  cache: false
  freeze: false
Check: a build failure stops the render. Results recompute from the inputs.

The report may declare these options in its YAML or inherit them from _quarto.yml. Source: https://quarto.org/docs/projects/code-execution.html (checked 2026-10-06). freeze: auto tracks source changes on project renders, not arbitrary external data changes. This lab keeps execution fresh instead of requiring a cache policy.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
The Analysis Codex Might Write
A cell to inspect in the report:
```{python}
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("context/measurements.csv")
assert df["run"].is_unique
assert df[["baseline_s", "candidate_s"]].notna().all().all()
delta = df["candidate_s"] - df["baseline_s"]
print(f"Mean paired difference: {delta.mean():.2f} s")
```
Check: the subtraction preserves pairs and the result includes units. The study notes, rather than column names alone, establish pairing.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
An Independent Numerical Check
Let \(d_i=t_{i,\mathrm{candidate}}-t_{i,\mathrm{baseline}}\) for pair \(i\). The mean paired difference is \(\bar d=\frac{1}{n}\sum_i d_i\).
For the supplied synthetic fixture:



Quantity
Value




Number of pairs, \(n\)
8


Mean paired difference, \(\bar d\)
−0.60 s


Pairs with a faster candidate
7 of 8


Run 4 difference
+0.20 s



Negative means the candidate is faster. These values describe the fixture only.

Computed from examples/ai-context/measurements.csv. Differences in seconds: -0.9, -0.7, -0.8, +0.2, -0.5, -0.7, -0.6, -0.8. Sum -4.8, mean -0.6. Ask attendees to calculate run 4 themselves before showing this check.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Turn 4: Correct an Overclaim
Suppose the draft says: “The candidate is faster in every run.”
Ask Codex:

Check “faster in every run” against the CSV. Identify any exceptions, correct the prose, and audit the remaining numerical claims. Re-render and show which computed values support the revised wording.

Acceptable interpretation: the candidate has a lower runtime in seven of these eight synthetic pairs, with a mean difference of −0.60 s.
Check: the report identifies run 4 and retains the synthetic-data limitation.

The flawed sentence is a deliberate teaching example, not an observed agent output. Use a real defect if the generated report is already correct.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Turn 5: Improve the Figure
If the figure shows only aggregate means, ask Codex:

Show every matched baseline and candidate observation, connected by run. Label runtimes in seconds and make run 4 easy to identify. Update the caption and alt text, then render the report again.

Check: you can locate the regression directly in the figure.
Exercise
Name one visual change that would make the evidence easier to interpret. Request it and verify that the underlying values remain unchanged.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: Questions Codex Cannot Settle from These Files
text:
Questions Codex Cannot Settle from These Files
Ask Codex:

What assumptions would a confidence interval require here? Separate facts in notes.md from assumptions we would need for real measurements. Explain what additional study information is missing.

Check: an interval cannot turn invented observations into empirical evidence.
The unit of analysis is the pair. Any paired resampling must preserve it. Repeated runs on one workload do not establish performance on other workloads.

This is a methodological critique, not a request to invent an inferential result. Any optional interval needs a justified sampling model and a verified methods reference. The fixture intentionally supplies neither a real sampling design nor an empirical performance claim.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: Turn 6: Adapt the Report into Slides
text:
Turn 6: Adapt the Report into Slides
Ask Codex:

Create slides.qmd with exactly 8 slides including its title. Reuse the report’s verified computation. Cover the question, design, paired data, result, uncertainty, limitations, and discussion. Use a dark Reveal.js theme and speaker notes for detail. Render and inspect every slide.

Command involved:
quarto render slides.qmd --to revealjs
Check: count eight slides and compare every number with the report.

Quarto slide authoring: https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/ (checked 2026-10-06). YAML title metadata creates a title slide. Seven content slides plus that title satisfy the count. Extra section slides count too.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: Turn 7: Fix an Observed Layout Defect
text:
Turn 7: Fix an Observed Layout Defect
If a figure and explanation are crowded, ask Codex:

On the Results slide, the caption falls below the visible area. Move the detailed interpretation to speaker notes and shorten the caption. Keep the figure readable and the total at 8 slides. Re-render and check the slide at presentation size and a narrow viewport.

Check: the entire caption fits, and notes retain the necessary explanation.
If Codex has no browser tool, open the output yourself and report the defect. Ask it to distinguish checks it performed from checks still needed.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Turn 8: Review the Whole Deliverable
Ask Codex:

Rebuild both outputs. Compare their numerical claims against the CSV, check citation targets and internal links, and inspect the figures. Review the diff and report the commands run, remaining limitations, and exact files ready for my review. Keep this work local.

Commands involved:
quarto render report.qmd --to html
quarto render slides.qmd --to revealjs
git diff --check
Check: the handoff includes source, dependency instructions, and rendered outputs.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Optional: A Research Website
From a fresh workspace with copies of your verified report and context, ask Codex:

Create a Quarto website in research-site with Home, Methods, and Results pages. Adapt the verified report, preserve its evidence and limitations, and copy the required inputs. Render the site and check every local link and its mobile layout.

Scaffold command Codex can use:
quarto create project website research-site --no-open --no-prompt
Check: navigation connects the pages and computations still use the copied inputs.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Optional: A Research Blog
In another fresh workspace with the report and context, ask Codex:

Create a Quarto blog in research-blog. Adapt the verified report into posts/paired-runtime/index.qmd with title, date, categories, executable analysis, and limitations. Copy required inputs and fix relative paths. Render the whole blog and check that the listing links to the post.

Scaffold command Codex can use:
quarto create project blog research-blog --no-open --no-prompt
Check: the post’s data paths work from its new location.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Different Outputs Need Different Reviews








Output
Ask Codex to change
Verify yourself




Report
Develop methods and results
Assumptions and computations


Slides
Shorten visible explanation
Readability and sequence


Website
Separate topics into linked pages
Navigation and mobile layout


Blog
Make a self-contained post
Context, date, listing, evidence



Keep the verified computation consistent while adapting the explanation.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Requests for a Larger Team
For a larger project, you can ask for bounded roles:

Have an evidence reviewer inspect the sources read-only, an author edit only report.qmd, and a render reviewer report visual defects. One lead should integrate changes and run the final build.




Role
Required return




Evidence reviewer
Supported claims and source locations


Author
Draft, assumptions, and checks performed


Render reviewer
Defects with slide IDs and viewport



Use delegation supported by your installed tool, or perform these stages sequentially.

This is an optional workflow contract, not a universal agent command or a claim that delegation has occurred. Assign bounded file scopes. Use separate checkouts or output directories for independent renders. One lead owns shared configuration and the final output. Tool-specific configuration requires current official docs.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Partner Review
Exercise — 15 minutes
Exchange the report and slides with a partner. Each partner checks:

One numerical claim against the CSV.
One assumption against the study notes.
One figure or slide in the browser.

Use the feedback for a plain-English revision request.
Done: show the original defect, your request, and evidence that the revision fixed it.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Lab Submission
Submit the report and eight-slide deck, their source files, the unchanged input copies, and the dependency/build instructions.
Include a short record:



Record
Example




Request
“Check whether every pair improved.”


Defect found
A claim omitted run 4’s regression


Verification
Recomputed differences and checked revised prose



If you find no error, report a check that passed. Do not invent an agent mistake.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Evaluation Rubric







Dimension
Evidence of success




Reproducibility
A partner renders using the recorded environment


Scientific reasoning
Pairing, units, assumptions, limitations are explicit


Provenance
Claims trace to data or verified references


Communication
Figures, slides, and links support the explanation


Agent supervision
Follow-up requests address observed issues



Which conclusions could a successful build never validate?

Installation and CLI guidance checked 2026-10-06. The prompts do not require a particular model.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
What You Will Build
A small Quarto blog with an executable post, created through a continuing conversation with Codex.
By the end, you can:

Describe a change and have Codex implement it in project files.
Read the Markdown, YAML, and code that control the result.
Check the rendered output and request a precise revision.
Review and publish your own blog.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Workshop Route



Activity
Time
Checkpoint




First Codex conversation and setup
25 min
A rendered document


Read and revise Quarto source
40 min
Executed output changes


Build a blog with Codex
35 min
A working post and listing


Review and publish
25 min
A verified public URL


Collaborative exercise
30 min
A reviewed contribution


Discussion
10 min
Explain what you checked




Audience: researchers and students new to Quarto. Prerequisites: opening a folder, using an editor, and basic terminal navigation. No environment-manager expertise is assumed. Teach the prompts live, then inspect the actual files and browser.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
How to Use These Slides
Ask Codex: paste the plain-English request into your Codex session. It can edit files and run local tools, subject to its permissions.
Commands: see what performs the work, or run the same step yourself. You do not need to repeat a command Codex has already completed.
Check: inspect an observable result before continuing.

Codex CLI capabilities and interactive workflow: https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/ (checked 2026-10-06). The prompts are workshop examples, not transcripts or guaranteed agent responses.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Before You Begin

Install Quarto, Git, and an editor.
Open Codex in your working folder, or use the CLI setup.
Sign in with an account that can use Codex.
Have a GitHub account and GitHub CLI for publishing.

The terminal examples use macOS, Linux, or WSL on Windows. Claude Code users can follow the same task prompts with their agent.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
A Folder for the Workshop
Terminal, once: choose a new folder outside this workshop repository.
mkdir -p ~/code/quarto-play
cd ~/code/quarto-play
codex
Ask Codex:

I am learning Quarto. Use this folder for the exercises. Check the tools available, initialize Git if needed, and work on a workshop branch. Tell me which folder you are using and what is missing.

Check: the session names quarto-play as its working folder.

In a graphical Codex client, select the same local folder and enter the prompt in the conversation. The CLI route makes the working directory explicit without depending on a particular app layout. Git equivalents: git init –initial-branch=main and git switch -c workshop. Initial branches can be unborn until the first commit.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
A Document from One Request
Ask Codex:

Create hello.qmd, a short HTML page for a student new to Quarto. Include a title, a paragraph explaining Quarto, and a list of two things I can publish. Render it, fix any build errors, and tell me which file to open.

Command behind the render:
quarto render hello.qmd --to html
Check: open hello.html and compare it with hello.qmd.

Live demonstration: send the request, show file edits and the actual render command, then open the output. Do not substitute the agent’s completion message for the rendered page. If dependencies are missing, use the setup prompt below.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
What Codex Did



Your request
Work to inspect




“Create hello.qmd”
A new editable source file


“A short HTML page”
YAML selecting HTML and concise Markdown


“Render it”
A Quarto command and its output


“Fix any build errors”
Further edits and a successful rerun



Codex can carry out this sequence from a plain-English request. The generated source remains yours to read, edit, and version.

title: Quarto Workshop
section: The Next Message Is a Revision
text:
The Next Message Is a Revision
Continue in the same Codex conversation:

Change the title to “My Research Notebook”. Add a section called “What I want to explain” with a placeholder for my topic. Keep the page short and render it again.

Check: both the source title and browser title change.
Exercise
Request one different revision in your own words. Point to the changed source and show its effect in the browser.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
A Useful Request

In hello.qmd, explain Quarto to first-year biology students. Use a lab-report example and keep the introduction under 100 words. Preserve my title. Render the page and check that the example appears.




Include what matters
In this request




Context
hello.qmd, biology students


Desired result
A short introduction with a lab example


Constraint
Preserve the title


Completion check
Render and find the example




These are useful details, not a required prompt template. Short follow-ups work when the conversation already contains the relevant context. Prompting guidance: https://developers.openai.com/codex/prompting/ (checked 2026-10-06).

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Quarto’s Job
Quarto combines prose, code, and results into a publication. Codex can write the source and run Quarto for you.



Source
Role




Markdown
Headings, paragraphs, links, lists


YAML
Title, output format, document options


Executable cells
Computation and generated figures


CSS
Appearance of HTML pages and slides



Exercise
Browse the Quarto gallery. Describe one feature you would ask Codex to add to your project.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Markdown You Can Recognize
Ask Codex:

Add a “Reading list” section to hello.qmd with a link to the Quarto guide and one bold phrase. Render it and explain the Markdown you added.

Source pattern:
## Reading list

Start with the **Quarto guide**.

[Read the guide](https://quarto.org/docs/guide/)
Check: a heading, bold text, and a working link appear on the page.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
YAML Selects the Output
Ask Codex:

Add a table of contents to hello.qmd. Keep the existing title and sections. Render it and explain the YAML change.

Source pattern at the top of the file:
---
title: "My Research Notebook"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
---
Check: the contents links lead to your section headings.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Formatting a Comparison
Ask Codex:

Add two tabs to hello.qmd: “Question” and “Evidence”. Put a short placeholder in each. Use Quarto’s tabset syntax and render the page.

Source pattern:
::: {.panel-tabset}
## Question
What am I investigating?
## Evidence
What would support the answer?
:::
Check: clicking each tab reveals the corresponding text.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Displayed Code and Executed Code
Ask Codex:

Add one displayed Python example and one executable Python cell to hello.qmd. Have each say hello. Explain how their fences differ. Render the page with execution enabled.

```python
print("This code is displayed")
```

```{python}
print("This code runs")
```
Check: only the executable cell produces a separate output line.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Codex Handles the Runtime
If the executable example needs dependencies, ask Codex:

Inspect the available Python environments. Reuse a suitable local environment or prepare one for this project. Render hello.qmd with execution enabled. Fix failures and record the interpreter, dependencies, and working command in README.md.

Commands you should recognize:
quarto check jupyter
quarto render hello.qmd
Check: the output exists and the recorded build command works.

The selected interpreter may require an environment variable or activation. Have the agent record the actual invocation, rather than teaching a universal environment fix. Optional reproducibility recipes are in the workshop repository.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
A Computation in These Slides
This cell executes when this workshop deck renders:

values = [2, 4, 6]
mean = sum(values) / len(values)
print(f"Mean: {mean:.1f}")

Mean: 4.0


Exercise

Add this computation to hello.qmd. Change the last value to 12, render it, and explain why the output changes.

Check: calculate the new mean yourself and compare with the page.

title: Quarto Workshop
section: Cell Options Control What Readers See
text:
Cell Options Control What Readers See
Ask Codex:

Hide the mean calculation’s source code in the rendered page, but keep its output visible and recompute it on render. Explain the option used.

Source pattern inside the executable cell:
#| echo: false
values = [2, 4, 12]
print(sum(values) / len(values))
echo: false hides source. eval: false would stop the calculation.
Check: the result remains visible and agrees with the inputs.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
A Separate Blog Folder
Terminal, once: use a new folder and a new Codex session.
mkdir -p ~/code/quarto-blog
cd ~/code/quarto-blog
codex
Ask Codex:

Create a Quarto blog in this folder titled “My Research Notebook”. Initialize Git if needed and work on a blog-setup branch. Render the starter site and tell me how to preview it locally.

Check: the home page lists the starter posts.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
The Scaffold Command
Codex can run the scaffold command as part of that request:
quarto create project blog . --no-open --no-prompt



Generated path
What to inspect




_quarto.yml
Site title, navigation, theme


index.qmd
Post listing


posts/
A folder for each post


posts/_metadata.yml
Shared post defaults


about.qmd
About page



Check: Codex edits the generated configuration without losing its structure.

The flags skip editor launch and confirmation. Run this command only in the new blog folder, and only if Codex has not already scaffolded it. Source: https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-blog.html (checked 2026-10-06).

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Your First Executable Post
Ask Codex:

Create posts/my-first-post/index.qmd. Explain a synthetic example of annual post counts: 2021: 1, 2022: 4, 2023: 9, 2024: 16. Generate a labeled chart in a Python cell. Add a caption, alt text, and today’s date. Label the data synthetic. Render the blog and check the listing.

Command behind the build:
quarto render
Check: the post appears on the home page and its chart matches the four values.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
The Cell Codex Might Write
One possible source pattern inside the post:
```{python}
#| label: fig-posts
#| fig-cap: "Synthetic annual post counts, 2021–2024."
#| fig-alt: "Post counts rise from 1 to 16 across four years."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.plot([2021, 2022, 2023, 2024], [1, 4, 9, 16], marker="o")
plt.xticks([2021, 2022, 2023, 2024])
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Posts (count)")
plt.show()
```
Check: the figure comes from the executable cell. It is not an invented image.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Preview and Render
Ask Codex:

Start a local preview of this blog and give me its URL. I want to inspect the post, the listing, and the navigation in a browser.

Commands for your own terminal:
quarto preview
# When you need a fresh output build:
quarto render
Preview serves the site while you edit. Render creates the output files. Neither command publishes the blog to the public web.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Feedback That Changes the Page
Continue the same conversation after inspecting the post:

The chart’s year labels show fractional years. Use the four observed years as ticks. Add a sentence below the figure saying these are invented counts for learning Quarto. Re-render the whole blog.

Exercise
Find one real defect in your own preview and describe it to Codex.
Check: show the before-and-after source and the corrected page.

The example names a possible defect, not an error guaranteed to occur in the previous cell. If the ticks are already correct, choose an observed defect.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
A Blog Checkpoint
Ask Codex:

Review this blog for broken local links, missing figure captions, and unsupported claims. Fix the issues you can verify. Render the whole site and report what you checked and what still needs my review.

Exercise
Open the home page, follow the post link, and return using navigation. Inspect the chart at a narrow browser width.
Done: the listing works, the figure is readable, and the prose labels the data synthetic.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Reviewing the Files
Ask Codex:

Summarize the changes and explain which files are source, generated output, or local dependencies. Check the diff and suggest the files that belong in a commit. Keep this review local.

Commands for inspection:
git status --short
git diff --stat
git diff --check
Check: inspect new files too. A normal git diff omits untracked files.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Publishing Preparation
Ask Codex:

Prepare this personal blog for GitHub Pages. Inspect its configuration, render it, and explain the files and repository settings needed. Show the destination and intended visibility. Stop before creating a remote repository, pushing, or publishing.

Check: you recognize the account, repository name, visibility, and content.
The next slide uses Quarto’s gh-pages method for your new blog. This workshop itself serves committed docs/ from main.

Publishing workflow: https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html (checked 2026-10-06). Approval here makes the classroom’s proposed destination concrete before students expose content publicly.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Publishing Your Blog
After reviewing the destination, ask Codex:

Commit the reviewed blog files, create a public GitHub repository named my-blog under my account, push the source, and publish using Quarto’s gh-pages method. Check deployment and give me the live URL.

Commands involved, after the reviewed local commit:
gh auth status
# If needed, complete gh auth login yourself.
gh repo create my-blog --public --source=. --push
quarto publish gh-pages
Check: open the live URL and test a post link after deployment completes.

Replace my-blog with the student’s chosen available repository name. Students complete authentication themselves. The agent should honor branch protection and use a PR where required. Do not run these commands in the workshop checkout. GitHub CLI reference: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_repo_create (checked 2026-10-06).

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
When a Build Fails
Ask Codex: include the failed command, exact error, and file path.

Running quarto render fails in posts/my-first-post/index.qmd with the error below. Reproduce it, identify the cause, fix it, and rerun the full build. Keep execution enabled and preserve the figure. Explain what changed.

Check: the same command succeeds and the expected result still appears.
Exercise
In a disposable copy, misspell a Python variable. Ask Codex to repair the failure, then explain the diff before accepting it.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Collaborative Blog Exercise
Exercise — 30 minutes
Work in groups of 3–4. Each person owns a different post on their own branch.

Create a branch for my contribution. Write a post about my chosen topic using the notes I provide. Follow this blog’s existing conventions, render it, and show me the changes for review.

A partner reviews the evidence and preview. Ask Codex to address the feedback. One integrator combines the reviewed contributions and publishes.
Done: each post has a working link, an identifiable author, and a reviewed claim.

Use separate checkouts or worktrees for concurrent writers. Avoid concurrent renders into one output directory. In a protected repository, use pull requests. An integrator may ask Codex to prepare integration, resolve conflicts, and run the full build, but must review the combined result before publishing.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Other Inputs, Same Conversation
A notebook:

Adapt my analysis.ipynb into a blog post. Preserve the computations, add the missing explanation, and verify that the rendered results agree.

An R analysis:

Create a post from my R script. Prepare the required packages, add captions and units, and record a working render command.

Use the same checks: source, computation, evidence, and rendered result.
